full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: This leave petition at the instance of the petitioners is directed against the judgment and order dated 8th November, 2009, of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in Administrative Tribunal Appeal No.240 of 2009 dismissing the appeal on the ground of limitation. 

 2. Respondent Ansarul Huq instituted a petition under section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act before the Administrative Tribun4 Dhaka being Administrative Tribunal Case No.145 of 2006 claiming pension benefits. According to him after completion of 57 years in service, he went on LPR with effect from 19th January, 2005 and thereafter, he retired from the service. After expiry of one year, the authority did not pay his service benefits on some baseless allegations. The Administrative Tribunal by judgment and order dated 3rd March, 2008 allowed the case and directed the petitioners to give him pension and other retirement benefits. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order the petitioners preferred an appeal with an application for condonation of delay of 7(seven) months, 14(fourteen) days. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal upon hearing the parties by the impugned order dated 8th November, 2009 dismissed the appeal on aground of limitation holding that the petitioners failed to explain the delay by assigning proper reasons. 

 4. On a combined reading to these provisions show that the period of limitation for filing of an appeal against any order or decision of the Administrative Tribunal is three months and an aggrieved person May prefer an appeal beyond the period of three months but not later than six months if he can satisfy the Administrative Appellate Tribunal that he has been prevented by sufficient cause from preferring an appeal within the period of limitation, The Administrative Appellate Tribunal has power to condone the delay of three months if it is satisfied with the reasons for not filing the appeal within the period of limitation. In the alternative, it can entertain an appeal if it is filed within Six months from an order or decision of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal after condoning the delay of three months. After the expiry of six months, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal has no power to extend the period of limitation.
